# ISSUE-164 implementation plan

Keep ordinary PR revision requests readable by released v0.7.0 coordinators while preserving explicit rebase semantics and current coordinator verification.

**Shape: Routine.** The incompatibility is an optional wire field whose ordinary value already equals the released coordinator's default; the fix belongs at the shared wire-request boundary used for serialization and recovery.

## What we know

- `revisionIntent` returns `work` unless given exactly one `rebase` argument (`internal/lease/carry.go:133`). Worker requests populate that value in both `BeginPRRevision` and `InvalidatePRRevisionEvidence` (`internal/lease/manager.go:1812`, `:1977`).
- `formatRequestComment` currently marshals the request unchanged (`internal/fork/transport.go:50`); `RevisionIntent` has `omitempty` (`internal/lease/fork_request.go:14`). Both public formatting and gateway posting use this formatter.
- `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go:16` already defines `releasedForkRequest`, `releasedCommentPayload`, `releasedCollapsedPayload`, and `releasedParseRequestComment`; `TestReleasedCoordinatorAcceptsRequestComment` covers actual posting, LF/CRLF, and faithfulness negative controls (`:86`, `:129`). Reuse this oracle. Its provenance currently names v0.6.1 and needs to name `github.com/supernovae/swarmos@v0.7.0` with relative source paths.
- The released source is available in the read-only Go module cache. The reviewer verified the oracle against v0.7.0 `internal/lease/fork_request.go` and `internal/fork/transport.go`: the request fields and strict parser match; `RequestMarker`, `MaxForkCommentBytes`, `contract.GateMode`, and `contract.Artifact` are unchanged. Keep the existing live contract types; do not copy them. Released `internal/fork/coordinator.go:479` calls `BeginPRRevision` without an intent.
- `Gateway.Apply` passes its request to formatting and posting (`internal/fork/transport.go:274`); recovery marshals that request and compares it byte-for-byte with the parsed posted payload (`internal/fork/transport_retry.go:118`, `:165`). Formatter-only normalization would break ambiguous-post recovery. Existing `TestGatewayPostRecoveryStored` (`internal/fork/transport_retry_test.go:258`) provides stored-then-error fixtures.
- `UpdateRebaseContext` emits `invalidate-pr-evidence` with both rebase intent and a rebase context (`internal/lease/rebase.go:163`), so its legacy rejection needs the same upgrade hint.
- Current coordinators pass the received intent into the lease manager (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:491`, `:511`); an omitted field therefore follows the same work branch. Explicit rebase retains its existing verification and evidence handling.
- Unparseable requests yield an operation-less rejection handled only after result correlation and trusted-bot checks (`internal/fork/transport.go:350` onward). `legacyCoordinatorRejection` already includes a generic workflow update hint (`internal/fork/transport_retry.go:185`); `TestGatewayOldCoordinatorRejection` exercises that path and adversarial result filtering.
- `make check` runs formatting validation, vet, staticcheck, and race-enabled tests (Makefile). The supplied snapshot has no accessible Git metadata (`git status --short` fails), so final diff inspection requires the implementation checkout.

## What we're assuming

- Normalizing only explicit `work` for the two revision operations is sufficient. Confirm with a table covering omitted, explicit work, and rebase inputs through actual formatted comments and the frozen parser. Preserve unfamiliar intent strings rather than silently interpreting them.
- Existing current-coordinator lifecycle coverage remains applicable. Confirm by running the full fork and lease suites, especially `TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle` and PR revision tests.

## Open questions

None blocking. The current generic upgrade hint may already meet the wording criterion; the implementation will make the rebase-specific requirement explicit and verify it through a trusted legacy rejection. No live GitHub or workflow changes are required.

## Design and exact touchpoints

1. Update only the oracle provenance comment in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go` to cite `github.com/supernovae/swarmos@v0.7.0`, `internal/lease/fork_request.go` (request fields), and `internal/fork/transport.go` (parser, extraction, regexp and constants). Check those declarations against the cache; retain the existing oracle and live contract types. Add an explicit `revision_intent` unknown-field negative control next to the existing “copy is faithful” checks. Do not add another frozen parser or duplicate contract types.
2. Add `TestPRRevisionV070Compatibility` to `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go`. For both revision operations, capture genuine current lease-manager requests with default and explicit work intent, then exercise public formatting and nonce-bearing gateway posting. Parse produced comments with `releasedParseRequestComment`. Before the production fix, record failure on unknown field `revision_intent`.
3. In `internal/fork/transport.go`, add an idempotent by-value helper `wireRequest(req lease.ForkRequest) lease.ForkRequest` that clears only explicit `work` for `begin-pr-revision` and `invalidate-pr-evidence`. Apply it at the start of `Gateway.Apply`, before formatting/posting, and inside `formatRequestComment(req, nonce)` before both marshaling and `requestSummary`, so public `FormatRequestComment` uses it too and summary and payload agree. The gateway's normalized request must flow unchanged into `postRequest`/`findPostedRequest`, outcome matching, and `legacyCoordinatorRejection`: the formatted payload and recovery's marshaled `want` must represent the same request. Empty intent already omits naturally; retain rebase, unknown values, and all other fields. Do not mutate the caller's request. Add a short compatibility comment. Leave lease intent normalization, request struct, coordinator code, local behavior, trust checks, and fencing unchanged. Extend `TestGatewayPostRecoveryStored` in `internal/fork/transport_retry_test.go` for both operations with explicit work: store the real comment then return a transient error, recover it, dispatch a successful correlated result, and assert `Apply` completes with exactly one request post. Include delayed visibility and retain existing adversarial recovery coverage.
4. Extend `internal/fork/transport_retry.go:legacyCoordinatorRejection` for these operations when `RevisionIntent == "rebase"` (including requests carrying `RebaseContext`) to say that the project's SwarmOS Fork Coordinator must be upgraded to a version supporting PR rebase requests. Preserve request ID, operation, original error, and existing generic hint for other requests. Never retry by stripping rebase intent or falling back to work.
5. Add `TestGatewayRebaseCoordinatorUpgrade` in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go` with rebase-specific rejection tests for both operations, plus an `invalidate-pr-evidence` progress-report request with rebase intent and `RebaseContext` as emitted by `UpdateRebaseContext`. Obtain the error by parsing a produced comment with `releasedParseRequestComment` and return it in a correlated trusted result with empty operation, matching the released coordinator. Verify immediate actionable rejection without state mutation or fallback; retain all existing adversarial tests.
6. Add `changes/unreleased/164.md` describing restored ordinary fork PR revision compatibility and the coordinator upgrade needed for rebase. Run the verification in TEST_PLAN.md and inspect the final diff in the implementation checkout.

Serialization normalization wins over changing `revisionIntent` because it preserves internal intent semantics and keeps all comment producers and ambiguous-post recovery on the same wire representation. Negotiation, coordinator admission changes, workflow pin changes, and broader protocol compatibility work are out of scope. No protected files change.

## Operator guidance

> Apply the reviewer's required revision exactly: do not add a second frozen parser; reuse internal/fork/compat_released_test.go (releasedForkRequest, releasedParseRequestComment, etc.), update its provenance comment to cite github.com/supernovae/swarmos@v0.7.0 and the relative source paths, put the PR-revision compatibility table and the coordinator-upgrade test there (or point them at releasedParseRequestComment), and add the negative control that the frozen parser rejects an explicit revision_intent. Keep the earlier normalization requirement: one wireRequest helper used by formatting, findPostedRequest matching and legacy rejection detection.

# ISSUE-164 test plan

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| Common work requests for both revision operations parse with v0.7.0; regression fails on current main | Add `TestPRRevisionV070Compatibility` in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go`. For `BeginPRRevision` and `InvalidatePRRevisionEvidence`, capture requests generated by the real worker lease manager with omitted intent and explicit `work`; emit real current comments and parse them with the existing `releasedParseRequestComment` in that same file. Cover public formatting and nonce-bearing gateway posting. Assert operation, issue, claim, PR, branch and applicable heads survive, and JSON omits `revision_intent`. Before the production fix run `go test ./internal/fork -run '^TestPRRevisionV070Compatibility$' -count=1` and observe unknown-field failures; after the fix rerun successfully. Do not substitute manually cleaned request JSON for produced comments. |
| Rejected rebase requests tell contributors to upgrade the project's coordinator | Add `TestGatewayRebaseCoordinatorUpgrade` in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go`, table-driven over both operations, plus `invalidate-pr-evidence` carrying rebase intent and `RebaseContext` from the progress-report path. Confirm current emitted JSON retains `revision_intent: rebase`, and `releasedParseRequestComment` rejects it. Use that actual parser error in a correlated, unedited trusted-bot failure with empty operation. Run through `Gateway.Apply` and assert error names coordinator upgrade, request and operation, preserves parser details, marks rejection promptly, posts once, and performs no fallback or state-changing operation. Run `go test ./internal/fork -run 'TestGateway(RebaseCoordinatorUpgrade|OldCoordinatorRejection)' -count=1`. Existing forged/edited/mismatched-result cases must remain intact and pass. |
| Current coordinator behavior for every intent remains unchanged | In the compatibility table, assert current `ParseRequestComment` accepts the emitted comments: default/work decode to empty intent (the existing work default), rebase remains rebase. For both operations preserve unknown intent strings rather than erasing them. Run `go test ./internal/fork ./internal/lease -count=1`, including `TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle`, `TestPRRevisionFreshPlan`, `TestPRRevisionFreshPlanOrdinaryUpdatesRetainEvidence`, `TestPRRevisionUnstagedRebaseResumeInvalidatesEvidence`, and cleanup/rebase evidence tests. These verify real coordinator work invalidation and rebase evidence behavior and claim fencing; no coordinator or lease semantics change. |
| Current coordinator behavior: ordinary revision requests recover after an ambiguous post | Extend `TestGatewayPostRecoveryStored` in `internal/fork/transport_retry_test.go` for both `begin-pr-revision` and `invalidate-pr-evidence` with explicit work intent and valid request fields. Script `CreateComment` to store the actual nonce-bearing comment then return a transient 502/timeout; cover immediate and delayed visibility. Assert emitted JSON omits `revision_intent`, recovery finds that same comment ID, dispatcher receives it and supplies a correlated successful outcome, `Apply` completes successfully, and exactly one request comment is posted (no duplicate or unknown-outcome error). This specifically catches formatter-only normalization. Retain all existing candidate/trust/budget checks. Run `go test ./internal/fork -run "^TestGatewayPostRecovery" -count=1`. |
| `make check` passes | Run `make check` in the writable implementation checkout. This includes formatting validation, `go vet ./...`, `go tool staticcheck ./...`, and `go test -race ./...`. Also run approved `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, and repository-wide `gofmt -s -l .` check to satisfy the compiled validation policy. |

## Fixture and scope checks

- Reuse `releasedForkRequest`, `releasedCommentPayload`, `releasedCollapsedPayload`, and `releasedParseRequestComment` in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go`. Update its provenance to cite `github.com/supernovae/swarmos@v0.7.0` and relative paths `internal/lease/fork_request.go` and `internal/fork/transport.go`. Verify against the read-only module cache; retain the existing live `contract.GateMode`/`contract.Artifact` types and parser implementation. No second parser, new oracle file, contract copies, network fetch, or runtime cache dependency.
- Next to the existing “copy is faithful” checks in `TestReleasedCoordinatorAcceptsRequestComment`, add a raw request containing explicit `revision_intent: work` and assert `releasedParseRequestComment` returns an unknown-field error naming `revision_intent`. Construct this control without the normalizing formatter so it actually exercises the forbidden field. Preserve existing negative controls, strict decoding, and LF/CRLF coverage. Run `go test ./internal/fork -run '^TestReleasedCoordinatorAcceptsRequestComment$' -count=1`.
- Check that a single idempotent, by-value `wireRequest` helper supplies normalization at `Gateway.Apply` and `formatRequestComment(req, nonce)`. Both `requestSummary` and marshaling must see the normalized request, and that same value must flow into `findPostedRequest` matching and `legacyCoordinatorRejection`. Verify caller input is unchanged and non-target operations/unknown intents retain their fields.
- Review `changes/unreleased/164.md` for the actual supported behavior. Inspect the implementation diff to confirm no coordinator behavior, workflows, protected files, validation policy, or adversarial tests were changed.
- Planning only writes active artifacts; red/green execution and full build checks belong to implementation. Tests use local fakes/Git fixtures and need no live GitHub coordinator, credentials, OCI runtime, or publication.

VERDICT: APPROVED

# ISSUE-164 plan review

The revised plan applies the earlier required revision. It reuses the oracle already in `internal/fork/compat_released_test.go` instead of adding a second frozen parser, updates the oracle's provenance to `github.com/supernovae/swarmos@v0.7.0`, puts the PR-revision compatibility table and the coordinator-upgrade test in that file, adds the negative control for `revision_intent`, and keeps one `wireRequest` helper for formatting, `findPostedRequest` matching and legacy-rejection detection.

## Audit

| Item | Plan / test plan coverage | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective: omit `revision_intent` when it equals v0.7.0's default | `wireRequest` clears only an explicit `work` value on `begin-pr-revision` and `invalidate-pr-evidence`. It keeps `rebase` and unknown values. | OK |
| Objective: send the field only for the intent v0.7.0 never supported, and fail clearly | `rebase` is kept on the wire. `legacyCoordinatorRejection` gets a rebase-specific upgrade message, and there is no fallback that strips the intent. | OK |
| Objective: regression test using the v0.7.0 parser | `TestPRRevisionV070Compatibility` runs real lease-manager requests through `releasedParseRequestComment`. The plan records the red (failing) run before the fix. | OK |
| AC1: work-intent comments for both operations are accepted by v0.7.0; the test fails on main | Covers omitted and explicit `work`, both public formatting and gateway posting, and checks that the JSON omits the field. | OK |
| AC2: a rejected rebase request names the coordinator upgrade | `TestGatewayRebaseCoordinatorUpgrade` covers both operations and the `UpdateRebaseContext` case. It uses the frozen parser's real error inside a correlated trusted result. | OK |
| AC3: current-coordinator behavior unchanged | Current `ParseRequestComment` is asserted in the table. The fork and lease suites run, and coordinator code is untouched. | OK |
| AC4: `make check` | Mapped (`check: lint race`, Makefile:44), plus the required-checks commands. | OK |
| Constraint: coordinator verification unchanged; field stays a parameter | Coordinator, lease and trust/fencing code are explicitly left alone. | OK |
| Constraint: changes/unreleased fragment | `changes/unreleased/164.md`. The name follows the docs/developer.md:558 convention. | OK |
| Protected paths | None touched. | OK |
| Shape (Routine) and rigor | Proportionate: one boundary helper, one message change, focused tests. | OK |

## Evidence verified

- `internal/lease/carry.go:133`: `revisionIntent` never returns an empty string. `manager.go:1812` and `:1977` send it, and `rebase.go:163` sends `rebase` with a `RebaseContext`.
- `internal/fork/transport.go:274`: `Apply` formats `req`, then passes the same `req` to `postRequest`. `transport_retry.go:118` and `:170` compare the marshalled request byte for byte. Normalizing only in the formatter would therefore break ambiguous-post recovery, so normalizing once at the top of `Apply` is the right approach. `RevisionIntent` is not read anywhere else in non-coordinator fork code, so normalizing early does not affect `expectedResultPresent`.
- `transport.go:371` sends an operation-less trusted rejection to `legacyCoordinatorRejection` (`transport_retry.go:185`).
- `coordinator.go:491` and `:511` pass `req.RevisionIntent` through. An empty value becomes `work` through `revisionIntent([""])`, so current-coordinator behavior is unchanged.
- In the module cache, v0.7.0 `internal/lease/fork_request.go` has no `RevisionIntent`/`RebaseContext`. v0.7.0 `internal/fork/transport.go` `ParseRequestComment`, `commentPayload`, `collapsedPayload`, `RequestMarker` and `MaxForkCommentBytes` (60000) match the existing oracle copy field for field and line for line. Only the provenance comment (which currently says v0.6.1) needs to change.

## Non-blocking notes for implementation

- The provenance comment must cite module-relative paths only. Do not include the absolute module-cache path, because it contains a local home directory.
- Keep `wireRequest` unexported. Make sure the public `FormatRequestComment` output and the gateway output for the same request are identical apart from the nonce line.
- When reporting the red/green evidence for AC1, include the actual unknown-field `"revision_intent"` failure output from the pre-fix run.
